title: _run_state.json -- pipeline run-state and backup tracker v0.3
description: The single source of truth for where a run stopped -- see harness-guardrails P7 and P10. Every stage's status is recorded here with timestamps; a crash or resume reads this file (via the DAO's get_last_passed_stage query) instead of re-deriving progress from scattered output files. After every stage passes, the orchestrator takes a full cumulative snapshot and records its path here -- one snapshot per passed stage, kept for the life of the run, never overwritten. v0.2: stage_name is an enum of the canonical stage names -- CASE_021's first full end-to-end run showed that free-form names silently fork one stage into several entries (document_processing vs document-pipeline, critic vs critic_v1) whenever a tool and an agent pick different spellings, which breaks get_last_passed_stage's resume logic and every consumer keying on stage_name. v0.3: (a) a 'skipped' status for optional stages (the Stage-3 indexing adapter) -- distinct from 'pending' (not reached) or a missing entry; an optional stage that never ran is recorded 'skipped', never silently treated as satisfied. (b) A passed stage MUST carry a non-null backup_path -- CASE_030 had policy_clause_processing 'passed' with backup_path:null while document_processing was still in_progress, exactly the half-finalized state P10's atomic snapshot-then-passed contract exists to make impossible.

human_input_status.description: Tracks P7's human-input waits. Entries are never deleted, only updated in place (waiting -> received), so the full history of what was waited on stays visible.

medical_gate_status.description: Whether the medical-appropriateness clearance gate applies to this run. Merge 3569d50 discarded the DAO half of the medical-review flow, so from that merge until 2026-08-14 the gate did not run at all: 53 cases exist on disk with zero medical artifacts, 9 of them with claim_analysis 'passed' through a gate that was not there. Restoring the gate retroactively would retro-fail completed runs whose evaluation results are already recorded, so it is scoped forward: a run state created from the restore onward is 'enforced', and every pre-existing run is stamped 'never_evaluated' exactly once. 'never_evaluated' is NOT a pass and NOT an exemption -- it records that the question was never asked, which is otherwise indistinguishable from 'medical_review_adopted: false' meaning 'asked and not required'. Absent on run states written before the restore that have not yet been stamped.

migration_history.description: Append-only audit history for explicit DAO-owned run-state schema migrations. A migration never fabricates a passed stage or silently deletes legacy state.

stage_name.description: Canonical stage names -- the ONLY values any producer (tool or agent) may write. Snake_case, versioned where the pipeline genuinely runs the stage once per draft version. If a new stage is added to the pipeline, it gets added here in the same change (D4). 'document_segmentation' is DEPRECATED and must not be written by anything new: once OCR moved ahead of the split (2026-08-05), segmentation stopped being a stage that runs before document processing and became a checkpoint inside it -- the bundle is OCR'd and redacted, THEN split, then its children are classified and redacted, so a run that recorded the two as separate stages could not say which was in progress. The value is retained only so runs written before that change (CASE_112) still validate; their record is accurate for how they actually executed and is deliberately not rewritten.

started_at.description: When this stage FIRST began an explicit orchestrator dispatch -- set once and never overwritten, so on a retried stage it is the first attempt's start, not the current one's. Incidental contract checkpoints do not set it. This is a MARKER-MOVEMENT time, not a measure of work: it is null when a stage passed without an explicit begin, and the span to completed_at can include human review, overnight gaps, and orchestrator delay. Do NOT use (completed_at - started_at) as a cost figure -- CASE_907 recorded 998 minutes for document_processing (an overnight wall-clock gap) and 0.0 for draft_report_v2 (finalize called right after the marker moved). Real work attribution comes from paired T13 trace events, never by subtracting these fields.

completed_at.description: When this stage was last marked passed/failed/skipped. Overwritten on each such transition, so it reflects the most recent outcome. Marker-movement time, same caveat as started_at.

current_attempt_started_at.description: When the CURRENT (most recent) explicit dispatch went in_progress -- overwritten only after the prior attempt reached a terminal status and the orchestrator begins a retry. A duplicate begin while already in_progress is idempotent, and incidental contract checkpoints do not move it. Present so a retried stage's latest run is distinguishable from its first. Still a marker-movement time, not cost measurement. Optional/additive -- run-state files written before 2026-08-04 omit it and remain valid.

timing_note.description: Set by the DAO when this stage reached a terminal status with no start marker ever recorded, so the gap is stated rather than left as a hole that reads like missing data. No start time can be invented after the fact. Optional/additive.

attempt_count.description: Count of explicit orchestrator dispatch attempts. Contract checkpoints inside one invocation do not increment it. P9 permits at most 3 attempts for a partial/failed stage before halt and user audit.

backup_path.description: outputs/CASE_XXX/_backups/step_<N>_<stage_name>/ -- null until this stage has passed. When status is 'passed' this MUST be non-null: a stage is only ever recorded passed atomically with the snapshot that backs it (see finalize-stage), so a passed stage with no backup is a structurally impossible half-finalized state. A stage later invalidated by an upstream change keeps the path of the snapshot that did back it -- that snapshot is a real historical artifact and is never deleted or rewritten.

invalidated_at.description: When this stage's recorded result was invalidated because an upstream input it was derived from changed. Set together with status='failed' and invalidation_reason by the DAO's cascade, never by an agent.

invalidation_reason.description: Why the stage was invalidated -- names the upstream stage and the artifact that changed (e.g. "upstream document_processing changed: redacted text rewritten for DOC_005"). A stage whose inputs moved must not stay 'passed': every boundary offset, evidence quote, and page mapping is expressed against exact upstream bytes, so a passed status derived from superseded bytes is a false claim about work that was never done against the current source.

allOf.description: P10 atomicity: a passed stage always has the snapshot that finalized it. finalize-stage records status=passed and backup_path in one run-state lock; nothing else may set passed.

description.description: What input is/was pending -- e.g. 'expert review of draft_report_v1'.
